reported_success.quote: In contrast to Piff and colleagues, we did not find a negative effect of priming participants to identify with a higher SES on their attitude towards charitable donations.

notes:
Explicit locator-study discrepancy: p. 20 reports Study 2, whereas input says study_r=1; target_match=false. Extracted the substantive charitable-donations test on that page (d=0.36), not the manipulation check (d=0.65). Authors state this substantive effect runs in the opposite direction from the original finding. Original p. 6 could not be independently inspected; no original statistics were copied from the replication paper.
Source follow-up: Original-only blind extraction from supplied published article; title and DOI match. Locator/study discrepancy: supplied study_o is 1, but p. 6 (printed p. 776) reports the requested printed d for Study 2. Retained the independently located Study 2 test with target_match false. Study 1 on p. 774 instead prints regression coefficients, not d. The overall Study 2 final sample of 81 is not asserted to be the analytic n of t(76).
